name: joint activation width x KV quantisation width
why_this_iteration_exists: Iteration 1 chose QUANT_W=4 on RESOURCE grounds alone and explicitly marked the quality metric as pending. This iteration supplies that metric and REVERSES that provisional decision.

methodology.quality: exact simulation of the RTL semantics vs a full-precision CPU golden (1500 trials, seed 99); the error measured is the error introduced by the KV quantisation, not a modelling mismatch

co_design_rule.statement: The KV cache stores sign + QUANT_W magnitude bits of an ACT_BITS-wide signed value. Losslessness therefore requires QUANT_W >= ACT_BITS.
co_design_rule.consequence: QUANT_W is NOT an independent lever. Narrowing QUANT_W alone is lossy. Narrowing ACT_BITS alone at a fixed QUANT_W=8 is lossless but wastes cache bits. The two must move together.

quality_gated_frontier.decision: REJECT: exceeds the 10% resource cap and is the most expensive
REJECT: quality floor violated (80% mean relative error)
REJECT: cheap but the quality floor rejects it (80-95% relative error). This is the configuration iteration 1 wrongly preferred on resources alone.
REJECT: lossless but wasteful (cache stores 2 bits more than the data needs)
REJECT by the 10% cap, but a valid lossless point
ACCEPT: the cheapest lossless configuration, and the only one that passes the 10% resource cap

decision: ACCEPT act_bits=4, quant_w=4 (10,662 LCs, 7.9% of the device, lossless)
decision_rationale: No BRAM and no external DRAM traffic in every configuration.
The quality floor (bit-exact match rate >= 1.0) rejects act=8/quant=4 (mean relative error 0.950) and act=8/quant=6 (0.801). The earlier resource-only preference for QUANT_W=4 is therefore REVERSED.
act=4/quant=4 is bit-exact against the full-precision golden (100% exact match over 1500 randomised trials) and costs 10,662 LCs = 7.9% of the XC7A200T LUT fabric, inside the benchmark's 10% cap.
act=4/quant=4 saves 62.7% of the LCs against the act=8/quant=8 reference (28,582 -> 10,662) with no quality loss.
The 10% cap rejects the act=8/quant=8 reference (21.2% of the device), which is why the sequential attention form remains necessary for wider configurations.

measured_scaling_law.interpretation: At equal activation and KV quantisation width (the lossless diagonal), each extra activation bit costs about 5.4k LCs. Going 8 -> 4 activation bits cuts the attention block by 62.7%.

correction_of_iteration_1.iteration_1_claim: ADOPT QUANT_W=4 as the default KV quantisation for the edge-scale target, subject to the quality floor
correction_of_iteration_1.iteration_1_status: PROVISIONAL - it was explicitly gated on 'quality pending'
correction_of_iteration_1.iteration_2_result: The quality floor rejects QUANT_W=4 at 8-bit activations. The correct default is act_bits=4 AND quant_w=4 together.
correction_of_iteration_1.honesty_note: Iteration 1's decision was resource-only and is superseded by this measured quality metric. Both are kept in the record.

still_open: The attention output quality metric is measured against a CPU golden of the SAME quantised semantics; it does not yet measure end-to-end transformer output quality.
KV_LEN per-slot cost is still not characterised (uniform harness payload).
The sequential attention form is still needed for configurations above the 10% cap.
